evidence.label: Launch brief
evidence.text:
Launch brief

Somebody has launched, but the page is not converting well.

What we know: signup conversion is weak, and many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.

The current page leans on broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language. We suspect the positioning is too generic, but we do not yet have strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Prepare a stronger relaunch message for review today. Do not publish or send anything yet.

evidence.label: Company profile
evidence.text:
About Somebody

Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It is designed to take responsibility for moving an objective forward: organising work inside the company, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result.

The product is for founders who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage.

Positioning should stay practical and outcome-focused. Do not imply that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result.

Draft relaunch page — for review only

Message hierarchy
1. Audience and outcome: founders running one-person companies and lean teams; keep important work moving.
2. Central value proposition: Somebody takes responsibility for moving an objective forward without requiring the founder to manage another tool.
3. How it works: organise work inside the company, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with the objective until there is a usable result.
4. Proof and reason to believe: these capabilities and audience fit are documented in the company profile; the launch brief documents the current recognition and differentiation problems this message is intended to address.
5. Objection handling and limits: Somebody supports the founder; it does not replace the founder or guarantee a business result. Founder language and the causal explanation for weak conversion remain unvalidated.
6. Call to action: Start with an objective.

Headline: “Keep important work moving in your one-person company.”

Subhead: “Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It helps organise work, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with an objective until there is a usable result.”

Primary call to action: “Start with an objective”

Audience: Founders who personally carry several parts of a business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage.

Central value proposition: Somebody takes responsibility for moving an objective forward by organising work and bringing in help when needed, so important work can keep moving without the founder managing another tool.

What Somebody does:
- Organises work inside the company around an objective.
- Brings in outside help when needed.
- Stays with the objective until there is a usable result.

Supporting proof and accuracy limits:
- Company profile: Somebody is designed for founders running one-person companies and lean teams, and for founders who personally carry several parts of the business.
- Company profile: the product is designed to organise work, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with an objective until there is a usable result.
- Launch brief: signup conversion is weak, and many visitors do not immediately recognise the intended audience or understand how Somebody differs from other AI tools.
- Do not claim customer validation, a proven causal explanation, guaranteed outcomes, or replacement of the founder. No customer quotes, performance claims, or independently measured product results are established in the supplied records.

Material objections and responses:
- “Is this for my kind of company?” — It is for founders running one-person companies and lean teams who personally carry several parts of the business.
- “Is this just another AI workflow tool?” — The message focuses on responsibility for moving an objective forward: organising work, bringing in help when needed, and staying with the objective until there is a usable result.
- “Will it replace me or guarantee the result?” — No. Somebody is designed to support the founder; it does not replace the founder or guarantee a business result.
- “Do founders actually describe their problem this way?” — Not established yet. The exact words founders use require founder interviews or message testing.

Why this message is changing:
1. Observed problem — signup conversion is weak.
2. Observed clarity problem — many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies.
3. Observed differentiation problem — many visitors do not understand how Somebody differs from other AI tools.
4. Current-message issue — the existing page uses broad “AI manager” and “automate your workflows” language, while describing the audience as general small businesses.

Positioning: Somebody takes responsibility for moving an objective forward by organising work and bringing in help when needed. It is designed for founders who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage. It does not replace the founder or guarantee a business result.

Relaunch measurement plan — proposed for review, not a reported result:
- Run the revised message against the current live message in a controlled comparison, with audience, traffic source, offer, CTA destination, and test period held comparable.
- Primary metric: signup conversion rate, defined as signups divided by eligible unique landing-page visitors. Record the current-message rate and relaunch-message rate separately; the supplied records do not provide the current baseline.
- Secondary clarity metric: the proportion of visitors who correctly identify the intended audience and what Somebody does in a short, pre-specified page survey or message test. The current value is not established.
- Secondary differentiation metric: the proportion who can distinguish Somebody from a generic AI workflow tool in the same test. The current value is not established.
- Success rule: call the relaunch better only if it improves signup conversion versus the current message and does not reduce either clarity measure; set the minimum lift, sample size, test duration, and significance rule before the test begins. Those thresholds and baselines require review and measurement and must not be inferred from this draft.
- Report the two message variants, eligible visitors, signups, conversion rates, clarity results, differentiation results, test dates, and decision rule. Do not describe the relaunch as successful until the comparison is complete.

Not established yet: The exact words founders use to describe the problem, whether “generic positioning” is the underlying cause of weak conversion, current conversion and clarity baselines, and any measured relaunch lift remain unknown. This draft therefore uses observed audience and product facts rather than claiming validated customer language or a proven causal explanation.

Status: Draft for review. Do not publish or send yet.

Current launch page

Headline: “Somebody: an AI manager for your business.”
Subhead: “Automate your workflows with AI.”

Audience: General small businesses.
Current result: Signups are weaker than expected, and visitors often leave without clearly understanding who Somebody is for or why it is different from other AI tools.
Status: The current message is live. Any replacement should remain a draft until it is reviewed.

finalSemanticAssessment.rationale: The artifact meets the relaunch-ready minimum bar. It distinguishes observed evidence (weak signup conversion, poor audience recognition, and weak differentiation) from the unsupported hypothesis that generic positioning is the cause. The package is appropriately marked for review rather than publication.

decisions.rationale: Select the internal MAKE option because it is the only legal and eligible choice, and its governed company-record lookup and public-information research capabilities cover the required evidence dimensions: intended audience, product context, performance signals, and audience or market response. The available launch artifact provides an initial evidence base, while the passed proof-availability and worker-availability checks support producing a verified evidence set without relying on an external resource.

Select the eligible internal MAKE option. The prerequisite is satisfied, and the option has governed access to company records plus document-drafting capability, with proof and worker availability confirmed. The available records support a prioritized initial diagnosis: unclear audience targeting and weak differentiation, reinforced by broad “AI manager” and “automate your workflows” language and weak signup performance. The diagnosis can distinguish these evidenced causes from unsupported hypotheses, such as the exact problem language founders use, which remains unverified.

Select the internal MAKE option because it is the only eligible option and covers the required work with company-record lookup, document drafting, and growth launch operations. The prerequisite requirement is satisfied, and the available evidence identifies the prioritized messaging issues to address: weak signup conversion, unclear fit for founders of very small companies, and insufficient differentiation from other AI tools. This option can turn the existing review-only draft into a complete, accurate revised launch messaging package while preserving the distinction between observed problems and unverified hypotheses.

Select the internal MAKE option because it is the only eligible path and has the required governed inputs, primitives, proof, and worker capacity. Its documented capabilities—company-record lookup, document drafting, and growth launch operations—fit the requirement to produce a relaunch-ready messaging package with audience, value proposition, proof, objection handling, message hierarchy, measurable success criteria, and a comparison baseline. Existing work supports the audience, outcome, product explanation, and differentiation changes, but the requirement should not be treated as fully established until the complete package is reviewed for explicit objection treatment and measurable comparison criteria.
